questions.topic: Dual-Tower Architecture: Encode Separately, Compare by Dot Product
questions.question: What makes document vectors reusable across queries in a bi-encoder?
options: The document tower encodes each document without seeing the current query
The query tower is applied to every stored document at request time
Both towers share weights, so either can re-derive the other's output
The scoring function rewrites the document text before comparing it

questions.topic: Dual-Tower Architecture: Encode Separately, Compare by Dot Product
questions.question: What is the standard bi-encoder scoring pattern?
options: Run one joint transformer over each query-document pair, then rank
Encode query and document separately, then compare their vectors
Encode the query, then decode it into the document's vocabulary
Compare the query against a centroid computed per document cluster

questions.topic: Dual-Tower Architecture: Encode Separately, Compare by Dot Product
questions.question: Why must an encoder upgrade be coordinated with the vector index?
options: The new model may emit vectors the index's metric cannot compare
Document identifiers are derived from the encoder's checkpoint hash
The new model can define a different coordinate space entirely
Approximate index graphs are rebuilt whenever any model version changes

questions.topic: Dual-Tower Architecture: Encode Separately, Compare by Dot Product
questions.question: What is the main quality limitation created by independent encoding?
options: Document vectors must be recomputed whenever the query distribution shifts
The two towers can drift apart because they are trained on different data
Scoring is limited to a single dot product, so no threshold can be applied
The document representation cannot adapt its token interactions per query

questions.topic: Dual-Tower Architecture: Encode Separately, Compare by Dot Product
questions.question: A new query service uses model v2 while the index still holds model v1 vectors of the same dimension. What is the safest response?
options: Block the mismatch and complete a versioned re-embedding migration
Serve both, since matching dimensions make the dot product well defined
Normalize both sets to unit length so the two spaces become comparable
Rerank the v1 results with v2 so the mismatch is corrected downstream

questions.topic: Dual-Tower Architecture: Encode Separately, Compare by Dot Product
questions.question: Vector search takes 8 ms but total retrieval takes 180 ms. What should be measured next?
options: The index's recall curve, since a low probe count inflates end-to-end cost
Online query encoding and the surrounding request latency
The stored vector footprint, since paging dominates once it exceeds memory
The number of shards, since fan-out multiplies the per-shard search time

questions.question: What does mean pooling produce?
options: One vector per token, averaged across the model's attention heads
A weighted sum of token vectors, weighted by inverse document frequency
One vector averaged from the eligible token states of the input
A centroid of the document's chunks, recomputed as chunks are added

questions.question: What does a token-level representation retain that one sentence vector loses?
options: The original ordering of the tokens as they appeared in the text
The document's length, which pooling normalizes away entirely
The vocabulary identity of each token before contextualization
Separate contextual vectors carrying local token-level evidence

questions.question: Why must padding tokens be excluded from mean pooling?
options: Their states are averaged in and distort the pooled representation
They carry no positional encoding, so the mean becomes undefined
They are shared across the batch, leaking one document into another
They inflate the vector norm and break the index's distance metric

questions.question: What is a key cost of late interaction over token embeddings?
options: It cannot be combined with a lexical retriever in a hybrid pipeline
It increases vector storage and the work done per query at scoring time
It requires the query to be re-encoded once per candidate document
It prevents any quantization, since token vectors must stay exact

questions.question: A long passage contains several unrelated procedures and small details determine relevance. Which design deserves evaluation?
options: A larger encoder with a longer context window over the whole passage
A lexical retriever alone, since exact details are lexical evidence
Focused chunks, or a multi-vector late-interaction representation
A summary vector built from the passage's headings before encoding

questions.question: When is one sentence embedding usually the stronger production default?
options: When relevance depends on rare exact terms appearing in the passage
When passages are long enough that pooling captures every subtopic
When the reranker is strong enough to repair candidate-set mistakes
When high-throughput candidate generation and compact storage dominate

questions.topic: Similarity Metrics: Cosine vs Dot Product vs Euclidean
questions.question: What does cosine similarity remove from a dot product comparison?
options: The effect of the vectors' magnitudes
The angle between the two vectors being compared
The contribution of dimensions whose values are negative
The dependence on how many dimensions the space has

questions.topic: Similarity Metrics: Cosine vs Dot Product vs Euclidean
questions.question: When do cosine similarity and dot product give the same ranking?
options: When the query vector is normalized, whatever the document norms are
When every compared vector is normalized to unit length
When all vectors lie in the non-negative orthant of the space
When the corpus vectors all share the same mean and variance

questions.topic: Similarity Metrics: Cosine vs Dot Product vs Euclidean
questions.question: Query [1,0] is compared by dot product with [2,0] and [0.8,0.6]. Which vector ranks first?
options: They tie, since both have the same cosine
The vector [0.8,0.6]
The vector [2,0]
Neither, since the query is not normalized

questions.topic: Similarity Metrics: Cosine vs Dot Product vs Euclidean
questions.question: What should happen to a zero vector in a cosine-search pipeline?
options: Score it as maximally dissimilar so it sorts to the end of the results
Substitute the corpus centroid so the comparison remains well defined
Store it unnormalized and compare it by dot product instead
Reject or route it, because cosine similarity is undefined for it

questions.topic: Similarity Metrics: Cosine vs Dot Product vs Euclidean
questions.question: An embedding model was trained with meaningful vector norms. What risk does forced unit normalization create?
options: It discards magnitude information the model learned to encode relevance
It changes the dimensionality the approximate index was built against
It makes the dot product and Euclidean distance disagree on ranking
It removes the model's ability to distinguish queries from documents

questions.topic: Similarity Metrics: Cosine vs Dot Product vs Euclidean
questions.question: A vector API returns smaller values for better matches, but application code sorts descending. What is the likely defect?
options: The index was built with a metric other than the one being queried
A distance is being treated as though it were a similarity
The query vector was normalized while the stored vectors were not
The API returns squared distances, so the ordering is non-monotonic
